# LiFePO4 is the better choice for most people

**LiFePO4 (also called LFP) is the better buy for nearly everyone.** NMC has one real advantage: it's lighter. But inside a finished power station, that advantage is small.

## How they compare

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Rated cycle life** | Typically 3,000–6,000 cycles | Typically 500–1,000 cycles |
| **Weight** | A little heavier | Lighter, though less than you'd expect |
| **Behavior if a cell fails** | Much milder | Hotter, more violent |
| **Price today** | Mainstream; now the cheaper chemistry per Wh | Mostly older or ultra-compact models |
| **Charging below freezing** | Usually blocked below 32°F | Usually blocked below 32°F |

**Cycle life is the biggest difference.**
- OutageMath's database of 54 models shows a median rating of 4,000 cycles for LFP and 800 for NMC ([outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- With daily use, an 800-cycle NMC unit reaches its rated limit in about 2 years. A 4,000-cycle LFP unit takes about 11.
- Check what percentage each rating counts down to. "4,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "4,000 cycles to 80%."

**Weight matters less than the cell specs suggest.** NMC cells hold far more energy per kilogram. But the inverter, case and fans weigh the same with either chemistry.
- In matched pairs like the Jackery Explorer 1000 and 1000 v2, the LFP version is only slightly heavier per kWh ([outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- Some LFP stations are actually lighter per Wh than older NMC ones ([unpluggedwatts.com](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

**Safety favors LFP.** In lab tests, LFP cells that failed reached much lower peak temperatures than NMC cells. They released smoke rather than flames. That said, LFP isn't fireproof ([unpluggedwatts.com](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). This matters most for a unit you keep indoors or in a vehicle.

**Cost now favors LFP too.** One site's listings put the median price at about $0.55/Wh for LFP and $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Cold weather is roughly a wash.** Some sites say LFP handles cold much better. The manufacturer manuals tell a different story: most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F ([outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [enoughwatts.com](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check the manual of the specific unit you're considering.

## When NMC still makes sense

- **You use it rarely** (a few outages or weekends a year). Cycle count won't be what limits its life.
- **Weight really matters**, and the NMC model is actually lighter than the LFP options.
- **You already own a working NMC unit.** There's no need to replace it.

Be cautious if an old NMC model is priced like an LFP one.

## Example LFP pick for home backup

The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) has:
- 2,073 Wh of capacity and a 2,600 W inverter
- A rating of 6,000+ cycles to 80% and a 5-year warranty
- 24.2 kg (about 53 lb) of weight, and it isn't expandable

It's $899 at BLUETTI's store. The listing says code **AFF5OFF** took $44.95 off on Oct 24, 2026, and checkout has the final say. This is an affiliate link from the deal site I found, so they earn a commission ([source](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)).

## How to choose

Pick a size based on what you'll actually run first, and treat chemistry as the second filter. If you tell me your devices and how you'll use the station (outages, camping, RV, daily solar), I can suggest specific models.
